briefdescription.para: Forces compilation of all member templates for one concrete service entity type.

detaileddescription.para:
Definitions live in this translation unit, so without these instantiations the route layer's shared_ptr<ServiceController<T>> registrations would fail to link. A "translation unit" is one source file plus everything it includes after preprocessing.
TYPE
Concrete service entity class to instantiate.

briefdescription.para: Definitions for ServiceController and its explicit template instantiations.

detaileddescription.para: The adapter methods are defined here rather than in the header; the instantiation macro at the bottom makes the concrete specializations linkable by the route layer. In plain words, this file contains the bodies of the small forwarding methods that were only declared in the header. Each body just passes its arguments on to EntityController, which does the real work. The block of macros at the end forces the compiler to build a concrete version of the class for each service entity type, so the route layer can link to them. This file has no logic of its own beyond that forwarding.

WHY THIS FILE MATTERS IN THE SERVER: Without these definitions and the explicit instantiations, the route registry's shared_ptr<ServiceController<T>> objects would be declared but never actually compiled, and the program would fail to link (the compiler would report "undefined reference"). This file is called by the route layer through ServiceControllerBase and calls into EntityController for every job. It is what turns the service interface into working, linkable code.

CONCEPTS TO LEARN (for beginners):
Explicit template instantiation (forcing the compiler to build a concrete version): https://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/language/template_instantiation
std::move / std::forward (passing values without copying): https://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/utility/move
C++20 coroutines (functions that pause and resume with co_await/co_return): https://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/language/coroutines
